newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Jurys expects another record year in 1996/7.
newsitem.headline: Jurys expects another record year in 1996/7.

text.p: Jurys Hotel Group Plc said on Thursday that trading in the months of November and December showed considerable improvement over the same period of 1995.
"Indications are that the year ending April 30, 1997 will prove to be yet another record year, subject to no unforeseen circumstances arising," Jurys said in a half-year results statement.
The hotel group reported a 39 percent increase in first-half pre-tax profit to 7.92 million punts and said this was achieved against a background of buoyant market conditions in Ireland and Britain.
Jurys said room occupancies remained high and considerable improvement was achieved in average room rates throughout the group, reflecting its emphasis on yield management.
It said Jurys Cardiff Hotel produced a strong profit contribution which exceeded expectations during the first summer period in Jurys' ownership.
Jurys Custom House Inn in Dublin opened for business in the first week of September and trading for the initial months has been "very satisfactory", Jurys said.

The group said it hoped to commence construction of a 168-bedroom Jurys Inn in London's Pentonville Road by April 1997. A 151-bedroom inn in Limerick, in southwestern Ireland, is due to open in May 1997 while a Belfast inn should open in April.
The group said it would also embark on a major refurbishment of the ground floor facilies in its Dublin hotel later this month, at a cost of 1.3 million punts.
